The '''2024–25 Ligue 1''', also known as '''Ligue 1 [[McDonald's France|McDonald's]]''' for sponsorship reasons, is the 87th season of the [[Ligue 1]] (French first division of football) , but the first for [[McDonald's]] sponsorship in the French premier football competition.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5359153/2024/03/21/mcdonalds-ligue-1-sponsor/ |title=French football league to be rebranded as Ligue 1 McDonald's from next season |work=The New York Times |access-date=20 May 2024 |last1=Rutzler |first1=Peter |archive-date=12 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260112235739/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5359153/2024/03/21/mcdonalds-ligue-1-sponsor/ |url-status=live }}</ref> It began on 16 August 2024 and concluded on 17 May 2025. The relegation play-off was played on 21 and 29 May 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ligue1.com/Articles/News/2023/12/18/2024-2025-french-football-calendar-released-ligue-1-ligue-2-and-more|title=2024/2025 French Football Calendar Released: Ligue 1, Ligue 2, and More|publisher=[[Ligue 1]]|access-date=20 May 2024|archive-date=12 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240912043307/https://ligue1.com/Articles/News/2023/12/18/2024-2025-french-football-calendar-released-ligue-1-ligue-2-and-more|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/La-saison-2024-2025-repoussee-en-ligue-1-et-en-ligue-2-pour-cause-de-jo-eg/1369991|title=La saison 2024-2025 repoussée en Ligue 1 et en Ligue 2 pour cause de JO|publisher=[[L'Équipe]]|language=fr|access-date=20 May 2024|archive-date=15 September 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240915095721/https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/La-saison-2024-2025-repoussee-en-ligue-1-et-en-ligue-2-pour-cause-de-jo-eg/1369991|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] were the three-time defending champions,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cp6gyyr372zo|title=PSG clinch Ligue 1 title after Monaco beaten|publisher=BBC Sport|date=28 April 2024|access-date=28 April 2024|archive-date=19 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240719134935/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cp6gyyr372zo|url-status=live}}</ref> and mathematically secured a record-extending thirteenth title with six matches to spare on 5 April 2025, following a 1–0 win against [[Angers SCO|Angers]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://ligue1.com/articles/l1_article_2298-psg-secure-ligue-1-title-after-tightly-contested-win-over-angers|title=PSG Secure Ligue 1 Title After Tightly Contested Win Over Angers|publisher=Ligue 1|date=5 April 2025|access-date=5 April 2025|archive-date=7 April 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250407203119/https://ligue1.com/articles/l1_article_2298-psg-secure-ligue-1-title-after-tightly-contested-win-over-angers|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Teams==
A total of eighteen teams participated in the 2024–25 edition of the Ligue 1. [[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]] and [[Angers SCO|Angers]] (who both returned to the top flight after one year's absence) were promoted after finishing first and second in the [[2023–24 Ligue 2]], respectively, and [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]] (who returned to the top flight after two year's absence) was promoted after winning a play-off against [[FC Metz|Metz]]. They replaced Metz, [[FC Lorient|Lorient]] and [[Clermont Foot|Clermont]] (relegated after one, four and three years in the top flight, respectively), who were relegated to [[2024–25 Ligue 2]].

==Relegation play-offs==
The 2024–25 season concluded with a relegation play-off between the 16th-placed Ligue 1 team, [[Stade de Reims|Reims]], and the winner of the semi-final of the [[2024–25 Ligue 2|Ligue 2]] play-off, [[FC Metz|Metz]], in a two-legged confrontation.

'''1st leg'''
{{football box
|date       = 21 May 2025
|time       = 20:00 [[Central European Summer Time|CEST]] ([[UTC+02:00|UTC+2]])
|team1      = [[FC Metz|Metz]]
|score      = 1–1
|report     = https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2025/05/21/france/play-offs-12/fc-de-metz/stade-de-reims/4652650/
|team2      = [[Stade de Reims|Reims]]
|goals1     = 
*[[Matthieu Udol|Udol]] {{goal|38}}
|goals2 = 
*[[Cédric Kipré|Kipré]] {{goal|52}}
|stadium    = [[Stade Saint-Symphorien]]
|location   = [[Longeville-lès-Metz]]
|attendance = 27,767
|referee    = Hakim Ben El Hadj
}}
'''2nd leg'''
{{football box
|date       = 29 May 2025
|time       = 20:30 [[Central European Summer Time|CEST]] ([[UTC+02:00|UTC+2]])
|team1      = [[Stade de Reims|Reims]]
|score      = 1–3
|aet        = yes
|report     = https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2025/05/29/france/play-offs-12/stade-de-reims/fc-de-metz/4652651/
|team2      = [[FC Metz|Metz]]
|goals1     = 
*[[Ange Martial Tia|Tia]] {{goal|57}}
|goals2     = 
*[[Matthieu Udol|Udol]] {{goal|78}}
*[[Alpha Touré|Touré]] {{goal|110}}
*[[Gauthier Hein|Hein]] {{goal|114}}
|stadium    = [[Stade Auguste-Delaune]]
|location   = [[Reims]]
|attendance = 20,392
|referee    = Eric Wattellier
}}
''Metz won 4–2 on aggregate and were promoted to Ligue 1 while Reims was relegated to Ligue 2.''
